newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stals says S.African inflation to rise more -paper.
newsitem.headline: Stals says S.African inflation to rise more -paper.

text.p: The latest fall in the rand is likely to push inflation higher, demanding a restrictive monetary policy, Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said in an interview published on Friday.
"Further increases in inflation should...still take place. This pressure has increased with the latest sharp depreciation of the rand," he told the weekly Mail & Guardian.
"This clearly demands a restrictive monetary policy and was an important reason for the increase in Bank rate to very high real levels.
"Future monetary policy will depend on developments in domestic economic conditions, such as the growth in domestic expenditure, money supply and bank credit."

South Africa's annual consumer inflation rate stood at 8.4 percent in September while producer inflation was 7.6 percent that month. The central bank last raised its key Bank rate to 16.00 percent from 15.00 percent in April.
